title: Activation sprint operating rhythm for customer pilots and release coordination
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Goal: Establish a repeatable operating rhythm for activation sprints that coordinate product, engineering, design, customer success, and sales for customer pilot launches. This ticket defines the cadence, deliverables, release-notes flow, signal ingestion, and success gates for the first 10 pilot customers.

Scope: scope covers initiation through 30-day post-activation. Not included: long-term pricing experiments (separate initiative) and Dedicated capacity commercial contracts.

Why: Recent pilots had fragmented communication between teams leading to delayed known-issues publishing and missed telemetry. A lightweight but explicit rhythm will reduce friction, shorten time-to-first-success, and give predictable handoffs to Sales/CS.

Outcomes: 
- A one-page operating rhythm (weekly sync, daily runway checks during week-of-activation)
- Release notes template and authoring assignments with explicit timetables for engineering/design/mktg contributions
- Dashboard and telemetry checklist (SLOs, core signals, regressions) wired before go-live
- Documented go/no-go criteria and rollback triggers

Audience: PMs running pilots, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success, Release Managers, Eng on-call owners, Design for UX artifacts, and Marketing for communication assets.
acceptance_criteria: One-page operating rhythm published in Confluence and shared with stakeholders
Release-notes template completed with sections and example content
Telemetry checklist implemented on the pilot dashboard (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, quality regressions)
At least 2 pilots run using this rhythm in 30 days with post-mortem created
All stakeholders confirm they understand deliverable ownership and timing
success_metrics: Time from pilot start to first successful integration <= 10 business days
Percentage of pilots with published release notes within 48 hours of go-live >= 90%
Mean time to detect pilot regressions <= 60 minutes (alerting configured)
Customer satisfaction qualitative signal (CSAT) >= 4/5 at 30 days for pilot cohort
